title: In Progress has no legal non-terminal exit: transitionTask allows only In Progress -> Done, and demote can't reach it
description:
Reported via opum-agent (orchestrator brief, 2026-09-05), from lore-cli's rebuild pass: the opum-workflow plugin's session hooks write their tracker note only when exactly one task is In Progress, so a repo holding several loses every hook write until it parks the extras. The orchestrator asked whether there is a legal parked/blocked exit from In Progress short of completing; there is not, and it is worse than a missing "parked" status - there is no way at all to reverse an In-Progress task's status.

Confirmed by direct source read. transitionTask (src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts:417-450) allows a status change only when the target sits at exactly configured.statuses.indexOf(current) + 1 - a strict, generic, one-step-forward-only walk over the configured status list, not a named "forbid In Progress -> To Do" rule. With the hardcoded default policy statuses = ["To Do", "In Progress", "Done"] (src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts:17,27-30), position("In Progress") + 1 resolves only to "Done", so Done is the *only* legal transitionTask exit from In Progress; the same rule also forbids any backward or skipping move for any status pair. No "parked"/"blocked" status exists anywhere (only an orthogonal, append-only BlockerEvent log that excludes a task from the ready set without changing its status - src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts:62-69,452-472,818-821).

quest task demote looks like the intended reversal mechanism (help text: "Demote a task back to an earlier status") but does not reach this case: TaskService.demote (src/application/tasks/tasks.ts:638-648) routes through moveTask(reference, "tasks", ...), which throws task_lifecycle_already_at_destination whenever the record's storage location is already "tasks" (src/application/tasks/tasks.ts:596-597) - and both "To Do" and "In Progress" tasks live in the "tasks" location (only "Done" relocates to "completed"). So demote can only reset a completed or archived record back to "To Do"; it cannot walk a currently-In-Progress task backward. Once a task is marked In Progress, completing it is its only legal status exit.

Scope: whether/how to add a legal non-terminal exit from In Progress (a symmetric backward-step rule, a dedicated pause/unstart command, or a workspace-configurable additional status such as Blocked) is an open design question this task does not prejudge - only that today there is none, and that gap now has a concrete downstream consequence (opum-workflow's per-repo single-In-Progress hook invariant cannot be restored without one).

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest task pause <id> moves an In Progress task to a new, non-terminal Blocked status, actor-attributed, with no config required to enable it
quest task start <id> moves a Blocked task back to In Progress, and also moves a To Do task to In Progress (superseding the plain --status transition for that step), actor-attributed
Blocked is excluded from quest task list --ready, and appears in quest task status-flow output and in pause/start command help

quest task demote requires an explicit --to <status> target; omitting it is a usage error with no mutation, and a target the ladder disallows from the record's current status is a plain error naming the current status and the legal targets (never task_lifecycle_already_at_destination)
The LifecyclePolicy can rename or disable the Blocked status for a workspace that opts out, without breaking pause/start/demote for workspaces on the default

Tests cover pause, start, and demote --to end to end, including re-promoting a paused task back to In Progress, and the near-miss regression: demote against an In Progress task (with or without --to) never mutates any other record
Design decision recorded on this task, attributed as the user's ruling, including the two rejected alternatives (config-opt-in only; a symmetric backward rule with no new status)

implementationNotes: Orchestrator ruling (opum-agent, 2026-09-05): the fix is a configurable Parked/Blocked status, not a symmetric backward-transition rule. Rationale given: opum-workflow's session-end hook writes its tracker note only when exactly one task is In Progress (a sound guard - it prevents a note landing on the wrong task); today a repo with two In-Progress tasks has no exit but Done, and opum-doc and lore-cli have already been forced into dishonest workarounds (archiving real unfinished tasks, getting stuck at three In Progress) to cope. A plain backward rule to To Do would satisfy the hook guard but erase the fact that work was started; a distinct Blocked/Parked status records it and gives task list --ready something honest to exclude. A dedicated pause command is acceptable as the implementation of that state, as long as the state itself (not just a verb) is what lands. FLAGGED: this is a tracker status-model/schema change on a published package (@opum-ai/quest), the same class of external-user concern raised in QCLI-159/QCLI-227 - recording the ruling here, but the actual design (new status name, default-on vs config-opt-in, interaction with --ready and configured LifecyclePolicy) will be put to the repo's own user before implementation begins, not decided unilaterally from this ruling alone.

Independent corroboration from lore-cli (2026-09-05), reported cross-session (not directly writable to this tracker): a live near-miss where running 'quest task demote' against a task believed to be In Progress (to see what the error looked like, expecting the same task_lifecycle_already_at_destination this session already found) instead hit a different, real Done task (lore-cli's LCLI-431, merged via PR #561, full final summary, 4 checked ACs) and silently succeeded - flipping it back to To Do with no confirmation, dry-run, or warning. Caught and manually restored in the same turn (edit --status In Progress, then task complete; final summary and all 4 ACs verified intact afterward), but the sharp edge is real: demote errors confusingly on its likely-intended target (an In-Progress task) while silently mutating an unintended one (any Done/archived task) with zero confirmation. Folded into AC6 above rather than filed as a separate task since it's the same command/lifecycle surface this task already owns.

2026-09-07, quest-cli self-corroboration: reproduced both failure modes twice more, once against a real Backlog-migrated In-Progress task (QCLI-196: 'quest task edit --status "To Do"' -> exit 6 'Illegal task transition: In Progress -> To Do'; 'quest task demote' -> exit 6 'task_lifecycle_already_at_destination') and once in an isolated scratch workspace against a task created and transitioned to In Progress entirely through normal quest commands (no migration involved) - identical two errors. This rules out the theory (raised by opum-agent) that the defect is specific to Backlog-migrated tasks missing a lifecycle event: it reproduces for any In-Progress task regardless of history, consistent with this task's existing root-cause analysis (transitionTask's position+1-only rule; demote's tasks-storage-location check). No new defect filed; this is the same gap.

2026-09-07: User's ruling on this task's design, relayed by opum-agent (asked with AskUserQuestion in its session, answered by the user directly - recorded here verbatim as the user's decision, not the orchestrator's):

1. A distinct non-terminal Blocked status, DEFAULT ON in every workspace with no config required; the LifecyclePolicy may still rename or disable it, but the shipped default includes it. Rationale the user accepted: it records that work was started, restores the single-In-Progress hook invariant fleet-wide, and external users hit the same wall so they get the fix by default.

2. Reached by `quest task pause <id>` (In Progress -> Blocked) and `quest task start <id>` (Blocked -> In Progress, and To Do -> In Progress). Both actor-attributed like every write. `quest task list --ready` excludes Blocked. `quest task status-flow` and command help must show it.

3. `quest task demote` requires an explicit target: `quest task demote <id> --to "<status>"`. With no --to it is a usage error and nothing mutates. A target the ladder does not allow from the record's current status is a plain error naming the current status and the legal targets, never task_lifecycle_already_at_destination. No interactive confirmation; it stays scriptable.

4. Tests cover pause, start, and demote --to end to end including the near-miss shape: demote against an In Progress task must not touch any other record.

Rejected alternatives, recorded for the design note: config-opt-in only (leaves the default broken for everyone), and a symmetric backward rule with no new status (erases that work was started).

Ships in the next quest release. Plan: QCLI-229 remains the single implementation task (its existing AC0-AC5 already anticipate this shape); no split. Target version 0.4.0 - a new default-on status plus demote's required --to argument (an error on a previously-accepted zero-arg call) is a CLI contract change on a published package, warranting a minor bump over the 0.3.x patch series.

Implemented on feat/QCLI-229-paused-status-pause-start-demote-to. Domain (src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts): LifecyclePolicy grows an optional pausedStatus field (default "Blocked"), validated non-blank and non-colliding with the main ladder. pauseTask/startTask move a task to/from pausedStatus using the ladder's working status (statuses[1]) as the pivot -- transitionTask's generic --status walk cannot reach or leave pausedStatus because it only ever indexes into `statuses`, which never contains it. legalDemoteTargets(status, location, policy) computes demote's legal targets: strictly earlier ladder positions when already stored at "tasks" (walking back), or up to and including the current ladder position when returning from "completed"/"archive/tasks" (un-terminating/un-archiving is legitimate); pausedStatus is excluded on both sides so only `start` exits it. demoteTask validates against that table and never resets to a hardcoded status.

Application (src/application/tasks/tasks.ts): TaskService.pause/start use the same single-file write() editOn already uses, scoped to active ("tasks"-location) records only via the same findTask(snapshot.tasks, ...) pattern. TaskService.demote(reference, to, operationId) now resolves the record's actual location first: a same-location write() when already "tasks", the existing two-entry writeLifecycle() move when returning from retention -- never treating "already at tasks" as an error on its own, only an illegal target is.

CLI (src/cli/main.ts): `task pause`/`task start` (actor-only, mirroring complete/archive). `task demote` split out of that shared branch to require --to <status> as a usage error when missing (exit 2, no mutation) instead of silently reusing the old hardcoded-target behavior. Manifest (command-contract.ts): two new "task pause"/"task start" entries positioned before "task complete" so the full-manifest CLI walk (test/cli-tracker-process.test.ts) exercises them while the task is still active; "task demote" gains filters: ["to"]. Contract surface (src/contract/tracker/index.ts, fixtures.ts): task.status-flow's data grows an optional pausedStatus field, kept in lockstep across the real manifest, its two internal exact-match tables (probe()'s consumer-side check and the fixture), per the drift guard test that caught the mismatch. Docs: command-help.ts and the overview guide (agents/guides.ts) updated; the "every lifecycle verb the manifest declares appears in the overview guide" test enforces this binding.

Scope deliberately not crossed: `task list --status`/`--exclude-status` still reject "Blocked" as unconfigured (resolveConfiguredStatus only matches the main ladder) -- filtering by the paused status by name was not asked for by the ruling and is a separate, later design question if wanted. LifecyclePolicy.pausedStatus is configurable only at the type level today, exactly like statuses/terminalStatuses already were before this change -- no workspace.toml wiring exists for any LifecyclePolicy field yet (composition.ts always uses defaultTaskLifecyclePolicy), so AC5 (rename/disable) is verified directly against the policy object, the same level every other LifecyclePolicy field is tested at.

Validation: bun run check green -- typecheck, lint (2 pre-existing unrelated warnings), format, layer:check, and the full suite at 418/418 (was 413/413 before this change; +5 net new tests, some existing ones extended in place). New coverage: pause/start domain semantics including the paused-status-disabled and paused-status-renamed cases; legalDemoteTargets across all four (status, location) shapes; demoteTask's validation messages; a TaskService end-to-end test covering pause -> start -> demote plus the near-miss regression (demoting one task never mutates an unrelated second task, and an illegal --to writes nothing at all); CLI-level coverage of pause/start/demote --to including the missing---to usage error, the illegal-target error text, and demote never reaching the paused status.

Not done in this task, deliberately: no version bump or npm publish. QCLI-229's ruling said "ships in the next quest release" -- cutting that release (version bump PR, npm publish, telling lore-cli what's landing per the cross-repo pairing convention) is a separate, later action, not bundled into this PR.
finalSummary:
In Progress had no legal non-terminal exit: transitionTask only allowed the next ladder position (Done), and demote's storage-location check was a silent no-op for any task still stored at 'tasks' -- so a paused, reprioritized, or mistakenly-started task could only be completed, never walked back, and the near-miss regression (demote silently mutating an unintended record) had no test guarding it.

Implemented per the user's ruling (relayed via opum-agent, recorded verbatim on this task): a new non-terminal Blocked status, default-on in every workspace, reached only via 'quest task pause <id>' and left only via 'quest task start <id>' (the generic --status edit can reach neither). 'quest task demote <id> --to "<status>"' now requires an explicit target -- omitting it is a usage error with no mutation, and an illegal target names the current status and the legal targets instead of the old opaque task_lifecycle_already_at_destination. LifecyclePolicy gains an optional pausedStatus field so a workspace can rename or disable it, verified at the same level every other LifecyclePolicy field is today (no workspace.toml wiring exists for any of them yet).

Landed as PR #282, squash-merged to dev at e1f6210. Public surface kept in lockstep: task.status-flow's data grows an optional pausedStatus field across the real manifest, both of its internal exact-match tables in src/contract/tracker/index.ts, and the command-contract.test.ts golden copy -- a pre-existing drift-guard test caught the mismatch before this shipped. Two new manifest entries (task pause/task start) positioned before task complete so the full-manifest CLI walk test exercises them while the task is still active. Docs (command-help.ts, the overview guide) updated; an existing test enforces every lifecycle verb the manifest declares appears in the guide.

Verified: bun run check green -- typecheck, lint, format, layer:check, full suite 418/418 (was 413/413 before this task; net +5 tests, several existing ones extended in place). New coverage spans the domain functions (pause/start including disabled/renamed paused-status cases, legalDemoteTargets across all four (status, location) shapes, demoteTask's exact validation messages), TaskService end-to-end (pause -> start -> demote, plus the near-miss regression -- demoting one task never mutates an unrelated second task, and an illegal --to writes nothing), and the CLI (missing---to usage error, illegal-target error text, demote never reaching the paused status).

Deliberately out of scope, stated rather than silently accepted: task list --status/--exclude-status still reject 'Blocked' as unconfigured -- filtering by the paused status by name wasn't asked for by the ruling. No version bump or npm publish in this task -- the ruling said this ships in the next quest release, but cutting that release, including telling lore-cli what's landing per the cross-repo release-pairing convention (task.status-flow's new field, demote's changed CLI contract), is separate follow-up work.
